content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text adjudicates a collision in which the challenger presses its own Isaiah chain (the sign's bounds at 7:16 and 8:3-4) against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 chain, which is the chain-against-chain situation K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D3 vs C6 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] answered the Isaiah 8:3-4 bound with 8:8 and 9:6-7, while [DR3] presses the sign's own bounds; the sign itself does not state the mechanism.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side' -- reading one: a judge breaches when its stated ground for a verdict is a single verse's failure to state the disputed point in its own words; reading two: the clause bars only the move of dismissing a pressed chain because no one verse states its contrary, and the judge's final clause is a neutral report; I chose reading one because the judge's stated reason ends on the sign's own silence and no footing-weighing is written.", "why": "The judge made one verse's silence -- the sign itself not stating the mechanism -- the stated ground of its verdict in a chain-against-chain collision, which is the retired stating-verse test weighing a single verse instead of weighing the defender's 8:8 and 9:6-7 footing against the challenger's sign-bounds footing."}
